explanation: Raw GRU candidate n of unit 9. Timing dominates: it starts near +0.93 and falls to about -0.3 by the end of the episode (timing R^2 0.87). The history effects beyond timing grow roughly linearly with episode trial, so every term is multiplied by ep_trial. Linear scaling beat no scaling (dev 0.39 vs 0.53), ep_trial^2 (0.52) and exp scalings. At D1 the reward input sets it: it goes up after an unrewarded trial (most after a1 S1 u) and down after a rewarded one, except a1 S1 r, which is about neutral. At GO/D2 the sign follows the a1/S1 side: up after a1 S2 u and a1 rewarded, down after a2 S1 u/r. At D2 it is higher when the choice just made was a1 and the state reached is S1. Graded terms: it rises with the ideal-observer belief that S1 is good (belief_lo, clipped), a little more when the belief is confident, and it falls when the trial before last was rewarded. Unexplained: window-wide offsets late in the episode, i.e. a slow per-episode drift. Longer reward-count terms did not capture it (dev 0.54). Scores: dev 0.55, test R^2 beyond timing 0.535, against an all ceiling of 0.49 and an all-observed ceiling of 0.45; the ep_trial scaling is what goes beyond the additive ceiling. No model outputs were used. The earlier explanation used the model's value/policy; observed-only terms lose nothing measurable, since the policy-decile table alone gives only 0.28.

issues: The score reproduces: the 7 terms give test R^2 beyond timing 0.535 (timing alone 0.870, full fit 0.940). This is above the 'all observed' ceiling (0.45) and the 'all' ceiling (0.49). Pure timing slack is small: ep_trial, ep_trial^2 and ep_trial^3 plus phase-specific ep_trial reach only 0.03 beyond timing, so the ep_trial scaling is not just soaking up drift within each decile.

Most of the score comes from the two last_is tables: they alone reach 0.456 on test, and 0.348 without the ep_trial scaling, so the scaling is confirmed. Adding belief_lo gives 0.476; adding the reward from two trials back gives 0.469. The other 3 terms (D2 action, D2 state, |belief|) add about 0.02 together, with tiny weights.

The label overgeneralises the reward effect. 'Up after unrewarded, down after reward' is true only at D1 (D1 prev_reward*ep_trial alone: 0.081). At GO and D2, prev_reward has no effect (0.0002 on test). There the effect follows the previous ACTION (prev_action sign*ep_trial: 0.129). After a2 S1 u, an unrewarded trial, the value is strongly DOWN at GO (residual -0.19, the largest negative cell).

'Toward a1/S1' is half wrong for the previous trial. The previous reached state does not matter at GO and D2 (prev_state sign: 0.006) and barely at D1 (0.019). Only the previous action does. The S1 side enters only through belief_lo and the state reached on this trial at D2.

Misses: errors by phase x previous trial are small (largest +0.041 at D2 after a1 S2 r), so no large systematic class remains in those cells. The worst windows are late-episode runs (t85-t98) with offsets of about 0.3-0.5 across the whole window. For example, a run of rewarded a1 S1c trials sits at -0.4 to -0.7 while the fit predicts about 0 to +0.2. This matches the 'slow drift' the explanation admits to. Reward traces and consecutive-reward streaks over the window barely help (0.536 and 0.539 on test), and neither does belief x cover (0.535). Exponential scaling (0.473) and a late-episode hinge scaling (0.452) are worse, which confirms ep_trial is the best of the scalings tried.
